Poland’s TOPR trials DJI Dock 4 for early mountain-rescue assessment

Relay stations, thermal imagery and a loudspeaker support reconnaissance before rescue teams commit to difficult terrain.

RoboticsTomorrow ↗4 November 2026English editorial summary
Story

A new rescue-service trial

A November 4 report says TOPR, Poland’s volunteer Tatra mountain rescue service, has begun a DJI Dock 4 pilot after using earlier equipment. Launching from a rooftop dock before ground teams depart can help determine whether assistance is needed and which people and equipment to send.

Reconnaissance and communication

A Matrice 5TD loudspeaker lets rescuers give instructions and ask questions, with people responding through gestures. Thermal and low-light imagery help identify headlamps and terrain. O4 relay stations on towers and distant peaks are being used to maintain links across terrain that blocks signals.

A trial supporting ground rescuers

The manufacturer’s 25-second battery-swap figure comes from controlled testing, and features depend on equipment and region. Daily hazard and trail monitoring are also being explored. No rescue-count or measured response-time reduction is disclosed. This is a TOPR deployment development, distinct from the earlier Dock 4 product launch.
